population: Randomly selected individuals plus six unrelated non-secretor individuals; ancestry not stated in the report
study_design: Molecular cloning and expression study with population genotyping
conclusion: About one person in five carries two copies of the FUT2 stop-codon allele, matching the non-secretor frequency of most populations, and the allele abolishes enzyme activity - the measurement behind this module scoring it 0.
provenance_quote: Approximately 20% of randomly-selected individuals were found to be apparently homozygous for an enzyme-inactivating nonsense allele (Trp143-->ter) at this locus, in correspondence to the frequency of the non-secretor phenotype in most human populations.

conclusion: The nucleotide-385 A>T change (Ile129Phe) segregates in an Indonesian family and, in two copies, gives a partial-secretor phenotype rather than a non-secretor one.
provenance_quote: This mutation showed a clear genetic trait in an Indonesian pedigree and, when appearing in a homozygous form, it was associated with the red cell Le(a+b+) and salivary partial-secretor phenotype.

population: Polynesians with the Le(a+b+) erythrocyte and partial-secretor salivary phenotype; alleles expressed in COS-7 cells
study_design: In vitro expression and enzyme kinetics study
conclusion: Expressed in cells, the 385 A>T allele keeps wild-type substrate affinity but roughly a fifth of wild-type maximal activity (Vmax 230 against 1030), which is the measurement this module's 0.25 activity value rests on.
provenance_quote: Comparative kinetic studies from cell extracts with mutated SewA385T and wild type FUT2 alleles gave similar Km values, but less enzyme activity was present in cells transfected with SewA385T (Vmax 230 pmol h-1 mg-1), as compared to those transfected with FUT2 (Vmax 1030 pmol h-1 mg-1), suggesting that the mutated enzyme is more unstable.

population: Sweden: 53 symptomatic and 62 asymptomatic individuals from nosocomial and sporadic norovirus outbreaks, and 104 Swedish blood donors
study_design: Genotyping of outbreak participants with saliva-binding assays
conclusion: Non-secretors were absent among symptomatic norovirus cases while making up 20% of Swedish blood donors, so two non-working copies protect against symptomatic GGII norovirus.
provenance_quote: Of all symptomatic individuals, 49% were homozygous (SeSe) and 51% heterozygous (Sese428) secretors, and none were secretor negative (se428se428), in contrast to 20% nonsecretors (se428se428) among Swedish blood donors (n = 104)

population: Residents and staff of an elderly nursing home in El Grao de Castellon, Spain; 34 symptomatic individuals genotyped
study_design: Outbreak investigation with FUT2/Lewis genotyping and saliva-based ELISA binding assays
conclusion: One non-secretor was symptomatically infected during a GII.4 norovirus outbreak, so the protection two non-working copies give is strong but not absolute; the module's wording is hedged to match.
provenance_quote: Genotyping of 34 symptomatic individuals regarding the FUT2 gene revealed that one patient was, surprisingly, a non-secretor, hence indicating secretor-independent infection.

population: White European ancestry, Great Britain: 8,344 cases, 10,008 controls and 3,360 families providing 5,182 trios
study_design: Case-control and family-based genetic association study
conclusion: The non-secretor genotype acts recessively and raises type 1 diabetes risk about 1.3-fold in Europeans; the paper also states which FUT2 non-working allele predominates in which populations - se428 in Europeans and Africans, se385 in South East and East Asians.

population: 7,582 pregnant women from the ALSPAC cohort, Avon, United Kingdom
study_design: Population-based cohort study of self-reported infections and chronic conditions
conclusion: A quarter of the women were non-secretors; they reported mumps and kidney disease more often than secretors. One working copy behaved like two for the outcomes studied most, which is the evidence that one working copy is enough, although for some conditions (asthma, arthritis) heterozygotes appeared intermediate.
provenance_quote: For some conditions, including asthma and arthritis, FUT2 heterozygosity (GA) appeared to confer an intermediate phenotype.

population: 4,343 ancient Eurasian genomes; FinnGen freeze 11 and UK Biobank, about 700,000 present-day individuals; intestinal enteroids from three donors
study_design: Ancient-DNA population genetics with biobank association analysis and organoid infection experiments
conclusion: Protection against viral gastroenteritis was seen only in people carrying two non-working copies, in the biobanks and in intestinal organoids, where heterozygous organoids were as susceptible as wild type.
provenance_quote: organoids from homozygous wild-type and heterozygous individuals had similar susceptibility to rotavirus and norovirus.

population: Ancient and present-day East Asian genomes; Biobank Japan
study_design: Population genetics with biobank association analysis
conclusion: The reduced-activity missense allele is essentially confined to East Asia and reaches about 40% there, and epidemiological work links it to protection against rotavirus and norovirus gastroenteritis.
provenance_quote: Epidemiological studies have identified a FUT2 missense variant (rs1047781-T, encoding I129F) that protects against rotavirus and norovirus gastroenteritis

population: 348 random blood donors in Bundang, Korea
conclusion: In 696 Korean alleles the se(fus) fusion allele reached 10.8% and the se385 reduced-activity allele about 7.2%, so non-working FUT2 alleles this module does not read are common in that population.
provenance_quote: From a total of 696 alleles examined, the frequency of the se(fus) allele in the Korean population was 10.8%. In addition, the new se385 allele was found in about 7.2% of the subjects, an unusually frequent occurrence compared to any other population investigated so far.

population: Taiwanese population groups: Minnan and Hakka Taiwanese and 11 indigenous groups
study_design: Population genotyping survey (PCR-RFLP) with Lewis phenotyping
conclusion: The weak-secretor allele Se385 is one of six FUT2 alleles circulating in Taiwanese populations, where it underlies the partial-secretor Lewis pattern.
provenance_quote: Six Se genes, including the weak Se (Se(w) or Se385) and three nonsecretor alleles (se571, se685, and se849) have been detected in various populations of Taiwan.

study_design: Population sequencing survey of FUT3 and FUT2 with CA19-9 antigen measurement
conclusion: se385 was the most frequent non-working FUT2 allele in this Chinese population at 40.19%, with se385/se385 in 16.2% and Se/se385 in 18.6% of 316 participants; the paper classes se385 homozygotes with non-secretors rather than as weak secretors.
provenance_quote: Se / Se , Se / se 385 and se 385 / se 385 were the main genotypes of FUT2 , with frequencies of 21.4%, 18.6% and 16.2%, respectively.
